ChengSimulationScaled.name: ChengSimulationScaled
ChengSimulationScaled.qfep_connection: A small society where role is destiny assigned at spawn — wanderer, grower, networker, predator, builder — and where unpredictability itself ships as an export slider called chaos_factor: emergence delivered with a management console.

dna.default: scenario=tour, field_display=arrows - tour reproduces the shipped 10-second carousel starting at Open Field and parking in animated noise, and arrows is the visualizer's existing visible state, so all 12 existing placements render identically
dna.was: sequence_mode was a private int the artifact declared as its own critical_parameter, driven only by a hard-coded DURATION=10.0 timer; every placement showed the same six-scenario carousel and no map could hold one field topology. The arrows were unconditionally drawn, so the piece could only ever be read as a diagram of its own cause. apply_grid_config() was an empty pass.
dna.note: field_display is the argument axis: hiding the arrows leaves the same 200 agents moving with no visible cause, which is the artifact's own truth line (purpose lives in the field, not the agent) staged as a question rather than answered by a picture.

FlowFieldMain.name: FlowFieldMain

KonigsbergBridge.capacity: PROVE why a bridge network does or does not admit an Eulerian walk by reading vertex parity.
KonigsbergBridge.description: Cross the historical city where graph theory was born. Four landmasses and seven bridges stage Euler's question, while degree labels and theorem panels show why no route can traverse every bridge exactly once. The artifact turns parity into something you can see and physically test, making impossibility a property of structure rather than player failure. It anchors the sequence by showing that topology can answer a question before search even begins.
KonigsbergBridge.gamwell_reference: Graph theory, search algorithms, string processing, numerical analysis, optimization theory, critical algorithm studies
interactions: walk the historical bridge layout
toggle theorem and degree labels
press E to trigger the Eulerian-path explanation
press B to explore bridge-removal scenarios
KonigsbergBridge.name: KonigsbergBridge
KonigsbergBridge.qfep_connection: Pure F in negative form: the odd-degree pattern forbids an Eulerian walk. The artifact shows that some questions are answered by structural parity before any search takes place.

affect_theory_visualization.description: Physics simulation meets affect theory — forces as emotional intensities, bodies as sites of felt experience. Where Deleuze meets Newton.

dna.default: individuation=named, locus=dispersed - both pure no-ops. named makes _affect_color return each affect's own Color literal untouched, so every StandardMaterial3D downstream is built from the same three floats it was built from before; dispersed leaves all four displays drawing exactly as _process always did. rng_seed stays 0 and capture_anchor stays false, so the RNG is untouched and the scene still contains no MeshInstance3D at all. THE SIMULATION IS NEVER GATED at any of the twenty combinations - bodies move, affect transmits, touches land and influence their neighbours identically; only what is drawn changes. Nothing in the 3 existing placements moves.
dna.was: the file had NO EXPORTS WHATEVER. The six affect names - joy, fear, anger, sadness, surprise, disgust - lived in one hard-coded table, picked a hue and a motion rule, and then stayed in the source; a viewer met coloured blobs, a bar field and some ripples, with the claim that any of it was about feeling nowhere on the floor. And the four displays were parked 8 m apart on four axes and drawn simultaneously, so four incompatible answers to 'where does affect live' were co-asserted and none was argued.
dna.why_these: individuation is the artifact's own open question made turnable: named is Ekman's basic-emotion picture, which is the picture affect theory exists to argue with and is what this file shipped; intensive is Massumi's pre-personal intensity, one hue and brightness alone, how much and never which; valence is the psychologists' circumplex, good-or-bad times strength; unmarked withdraws the colour key entirely and leaves the simulation running, which asks the brief's question directly - without the naming, is there anything here you would call an affect? The deformations still differ at unmarked, because the MOTION rule is named too, and that is the point: the question is only a question if the behaviour survives.
dna.declined_words: evidence (result/trace/longhand/axiom) and disclosure (oracle/tally/ledger/works/origin) were both considered and both refused. They ask how much of a DERIVATION or a MECHANISM is on show, and this artifact has neither: there are no generations to ghost, no string to write out longhand, no counts, no ledger and no seed on display. Three of evidence's four values and three of disclosure's five would have named organs this piece does not have - the folding_past mistake, taking a word without its answers.
dna.fixture_why: TWO BENCH FACTS, both about the capture and neither about the design. (1) Every body, particle, pillar and ripple in this artifact is a CSGShape3D, and the sweep's AABB walk counts MeshInstance3D and MultiMeshInstance3D ONLY. Finding neither it falls back to a 1 m box at the origin - and all four displays are parked 8 m out, so it would frame empty air and score both axes dead. capture_anchor builds one BoxMesh on layers = 0 (rendered by no camera, measured by the walk) sized 26 x 20 x 20 from the container offsets and the clamps in apply_emotional_physics. It is OFF by default because a mesh that size would also change what the grid's auto-grounding measures for the 3 placements. (2) initialize_emotional_bodies picks six positions, six sizes, six responsivenesses and six permeabilities with randf_range, so unseeded variants are six different crowds.
dna.not_an_axis: the affects table's intensity and transmission numbers are magnitudes; the flow speeds, the 0.5 s touch cadence, the 3 s ripple life and every sin(time * k) deformation are TIME, which one still cannot hold.
dna.found_not_fixed: update_emotional_states calls affects.find(func(a): return a.name == affect_name), which passes a Callable to Array.find and therefore always returns -1, so the temporal variation term is sin(time * 0.5 - 1) for all six affects instead of six phase-shifted ones. Pre-existing, untouched: fixing it would change what the 3 placements do, which is not what a promotion is for.

affect_theory_visualization.name: Affect Theory Visualization
affect_theory_visualization.qfep_connection: Deleuze as lookup table: joy transmits at 0.8, sadness at 0.3, and every body carries a boundary_permeability float. The earnest quantification is the exhibit — precisely what affect theory says escapes measure is here assigned a number and simulated anyway.

albers_wall_gallery.description: White gallery wall with 98 Josef Albers-inspired canvases and spotlights.
albers_wall_gallery.name: albers_wall_gallery

algorithm_overview.description: Interactive 2D flowchart visualization showing the complete learning progression through various algorithm categories and their relationships
algorithm_overview.name: Algorithm Learning Overview
algorithm_overview.qfep_connection: The curriculum drawn as a hand-coded flowchart of itself, node names hardcoded and already typo-drifted from the maps they point to. A self-portrait that shows how fast a map of the territory becomes a map of the moment it was made.

algorithmic_bias.description: Visualization of how algorithms encode and amplify social biases. Training data reflects existing inequalities, models learn to reproduce them — making structural discrimination computational.
algorithmic_bias.name: Algorithmic Bias
algorithmic_bias.qfep_connection: Discrimination is not an emergent mystery here but three legible lines: group A receives its errors as false positives, group B as false negatives, and B's confidence is multiplied by a hard-coded 0.7. The scandal is how little code an unfair world needs before it reads as statistics.

algorithmic_bias_visualization.description: Extended algorithmic bias exploration with interactive parameters. Adjust training data distributions, observe how bias propagates through model predictions, and see debiasing strategies in action.
algorithmic_bias_visualization.name: Algorithmic Bias Visualization
algorithmic_bias_visualization.qfep_connection: The injustice runs on a clock, not on data — bias_level = time × 0.08, rising regardless of what the particles do. Half against its own intent, it demonstrates that a fairness meter can be pure theater: the indicator moves whether or not anything unjust was ever computed.

astar.description: Advanced pathfinding comparison — Jump Point Search (pruned A* with symmetry breaking), Theta* (any-angle line-of-sight paths), and side-by-side algorithm comparison on the same randomized grid. ImmediateMesh visualization of open/closed sets, jump points, line-of-sight checks, and final paths with per-algorithm statistics.
astar.name: A* Pathfinding
astar.qfep_connection: Three definitions of shortest contest the same randomized grid: plain A* expands everything, JPS proves whole corridors redundant and leaps them, Theta* abandons right angles wherever line-of-sight permits. The path was never in the terrain — it is a property of which moves the algorithm lets itself think.

dna_declined.by: hand promotion pass, after the runner refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS
dna_declined.not_a_dna_block_on_purpose: artifact_dna_research.py line 253 reads bool(entry['dna']) as 'declared', so an empty or axis-less dna block would enter the ledger as a promotion. Same convention as throw_ball, grid3d_force_directed and audio_catalog_tablet.
dna_declined.it_does_build: NOT the tile_meander_floor case. The .tscn root is a Node3D carrying AudioEffects.gd, and _process builds six panels every frame: ReverbVisualization at x=-10 (eight orbiting reflection spheres inside a translucent chamber), DelayVisualization at x=-3 (eight decaying spheres travelling a 4 m rail), ChorusVisualization at x=+4 (six hue-ramped voices), DistortionVisualization at x=+11 (32 input points against 32 tanh-shaped output points), EffectChain at y=+8 (six labelled boxes with arrows) and FrequencyAnalysis at y=-8 (sixteen spectrum bars). Re-implemented and measured, the true extent is 25.76 x 16.40 x 3.91 m centred at (0.12, 0.20, 0.00). There is plenty of picture. The decline is about whether anything can be said ABOUT it.
dna_declined.axes_considered: TWO, both real, both the artifact's own hard-coded categorical vocabulary rather than invented. (1) `theme` = queer | sci_fi | cyberpunk | epic - theme_sequence and theme_profiles, four named 13-parameter presets, today advanced on a 16 s timer by update_theme_cycle. Promoting it is a clean two-line change whose default preserves exactly (_ready already applies theme_sequence[0], and starting the cycle at a different index still visits all four). (2) `spectrum` = clean | distortion | chorus | reverb - the `match int(time) % 4` inside show_frequency_analysis, four named claims about what each effect does to a spectrum, today swapped once per second with nothing on screen saying which is showing.
dna_declined.reason: THE BENCH'S OWN NOISE ON THIS ARTIFACT IS LARGER THAN EITHER AXIS. Every visible node here is queue_free'd and rebuilt each _process frame and positioned from the free-running `time` accumulator - reverb reflections orbit at 2 rad/s, delay spheres travel at 2 m/s, chain emission pulses at 4 rad/s, spectrum bars breathe at 2 rad/s. Each sweep variant is a FRESH instance settled for SETTLE seconds of headless wall clock, so the shutter time differs between tiles by whatever the frame pacing did. Holding the axis CONSTANT and varying only the shutter, three frames of drift (50 ms) already moves the picture 1.8x as much as switching theme does. This is not the documented 'time-domain axis' trap - neither axis is a rate. It is a worse relative: a per-frame-rebuilt SCENE, which poisons every axis declared on it. The failure mode is the dangerous direction, too: a noisier run scores HIGHER, so 400 ms of pacing drift alone returns a confident BITES verdict about nothing.
dna_declined.measurement: Computed by re-implementing all six visualize_* functions, update_effect_parameters, capture_config_sweep's camera (RES 760, FOV 34, YAW 0.62, PITCH -0.26, PAD 1.9, union AABB) and artifact_dna_critic's own load_img/diff at 160x160 with per-frame background neutralisation. Whole-bench anchor, framing 0.45 (span 26.3 m), cropped to the subject bbox. SIGNAL, theme varied at an identical shutter: frame 0.27% / focus 5.32%, WEAK - and queer vs epic is 2.03% focus, UNDER the 3.0% INERT floor, so the four-value axis is really 3.5 values with a twin. NOISE, theme held at queer and only the shutter varying: 16 ms (one frame at 60 fps) 3.13%, 50 ms 9.40%, 150 ms 25.43% (LOCAL), 400 ms 46.54% (BITES). Fifty milliseconds of pacing beats the entire axis. The `spectrum` axis is stronger and fails the same test: 8.27% focus whole-bench, 16.27% (LOCAL) if the camera is anchored on the spectrum panel alone - but at that same anchor 50 ms of shutter jitter with the regime HELD returns 13.96%, which is 86% of the signal, and one frame returns 5.09%. Both axes are inside their own error bar.
dna_declined.and_the_vocabulary_is_mostly_audio: Of the 13 parameters in each theme profile, SEVEN never reach a pixel - base_frequency, sparkle and noise feed generate_input_signal, whose input_signal array is filled and then read by no visualiser at all, and reverb_damping, reverb_mix, delay_mix and chorus_mix are read only inside generate_audio_samples. chorus_depth is a delay in SECONDS (0.0035-0.006) and moves geometry by at most 18 mm. That leaves four visible: reverb_size (chamber radius 1.76-1.94 m), delay_time (tap spacing), delay_feedback (tail brightness) and distortion_drive (tanh curvature) - and update_effect_parameters wobbles each of them every frame by a sin() term worth 18-28% of the whole theme spread. A tile labelled `cyberpunk` would differ from `epic` by a slightly smaller sphere and differently spaced orange dots, while the thing that actually makes it cyberpunk - a 140 Hz fundamental against 260, 0.25 noise against 0.1 - is inaudible in a PNG. That is SoundscapeRadioRack's refusal of station_width: real, audible, invisible.
dna_declined.harness_finding: WITHOUT A FIXTURE THIS ARTIFACT PHOTOGRAPHS AS EMPTY BACKGROUND, and nothing would report that. Every body here is CSG - CSGSphere3D, CSGBox3D, CSGCylinder3D - and capture_config_sweep._subtree_aabb counts MeshInstance3D and MultiMeshInstance3D only, so it measures nothing and returns its fallback AABB(-0.5, 0, -0.5, 1, 1, 1). That is 1.732 long, so it never trips the `size.length() < 0.001` rescue either. The camera lands 5.38 m out with a 3.29 m window on the WORLD ORIGIN, where this artifact has nothing: the nearest geometry is the right-hand end of the delay rail at x = -1. Same class as the wavefunctions and randomness notes; a dna.fixture.capture_anchor (one layers=0 BoxMesh at the true extent, default off) would be the fix, and all measurements above assume one. Grounding is unaffected either way: GridInteractablesComponent._compute_local_aabb does walk CSGShape3D, but the six containers are still EMPTY when it runs (they are populated in _process, not _ready), so it returns a zero AABB and _auto_ground_artifact returns at its 'No measurable geometry' guard. This artifact has never been grounded.
dna_declined.second_finding: visualize_chorus_effect has a unit error. chorus_depth is a modulation delay in seconds, used correctly as `(0.01 + chorus_depth) * sample_rate` in the audio path, but the visualiser spends it as a world-space offset: `modulation = sin(lfo_phase) * chorus_depth` then `position.x = modulation * 3`. Peak displacement is 18 mm, so the six voices the panel exists to show as 'modulated delay lines' stand in a motionless vertical stack. The panel draws none of what its own comments describe. A defect to decide about, not an axis to declare - fixing it would change what all 3 placements look like.
dna_declined.third_finding: spatial_needs.footprint_cells is 1 with 2 cells of clearance, and the parameters block says footprint [1,1,1], while the top-level footprint says [22,24,21] and the measured extent is 25.76 x 16.40 m. The three placements (Gallery_Misc, Gallery_Misc_Placed, Grown_MultiDisplay, all bare tokens with no config keys) each stand a 26-metre bench in a one-cell slot. Same class as grid3d_force_directed overrunning its declared bounds.
dna_declined.what_would_change_this: Pin the clock. An export that freezes `time` at a declared value under a fixture - force_directed_layout's warmup_steps + time_scale pattern - removes the noise floor entirely and makes `spectrum` measurable at about 16% focus panel-framed. It was NOT done here because it does not rescue the artifact, only the measurement: with the noise gone `theme` is still WEAK at 5.32% with a dead pair, `spectrum` still needs the camera on one panel of six, and the default of either has to stay `cycle` (both behaviours are timer-driven in every live placement), which twins with whichever value the pinned shutter lands on. Four new mechanisms - time pin, capture anchor, framing hint, axis export - on a 626-line script, to land a LOCAL verdict on a sixth of the object about a knob whose default duplicates one of its own values. The prior repair is the per-frame rebuild itself: this artifact reconstructs roughly 150 CSG nodes every frame, which is both the performance defect and the reason nothing about it holds still long enough to be compared.

audio_effects.name: audio_effects
audio_effects.qfep_connection: A mood is a patch here: 'queer' is a dictionary of thirteen floats — base frequency 220, sparkle 0.7 — cycled every sixteen seconds into 'sci_fi' and 'cyberpunk' through the same reverb and delay buffers. Identity as a point in effect-parameter space, interpolated on a timer.

Every placement showed the god's-eye view; the compressed perspective the artifact exists to deliver was reachable only by grabbing a VR slider, and appeared in no capture, gallery or still.
dna.note: Hero artifact of postfoundationscrisis, the spine-terminal sequence, where it recurs across three maps.

bias_from_inside.description: Visualizes a word embedding space from the perspective of a marginalized term. Instead of the usual god's-eye view, this artifact places you INSIDE the compressed region. A slider shifts between default perspective (everything looks evenly distributed) and compressed perspective (reveals how uneven the space really is).
bias_from_inside.name: Bias From Inside

boid_flocking.description: Emergent flocking behavior simulation using Craig Reynolds' boids algorithm
boid_flocking.name: Boid Flocking
boid_flocking.qfep_connection: Reynolds' three commandments — separate, align, cohere — and nothing else. No leader, no plan, no bird knows the flock exists, and the flock exists. The chapter's founding demonstration that coordination is not commanded but *emergent*: intelligence as a property of the between.

boid_manager.description: f_i = Σ(neighbor_j)[separate(i,j) + align(vel_j) + cohere(pos_j)] — three weighted averages over a local neighborhood
boid_manager.name: boid_manager

boids_2d_in_3d.name: boids_2d_in_3d
boids_2d_in_3d.qfep_connection: The flat textbook flock stood up in the room — 2D boids rendered in 3D space, the diagram and the phenomenon sharing an enclosure so the eye can move between the explanation and the murmuration.

booleans.name: booleans
booleans.qfep_connection: Three verdicts on the same pair of bodies stand as sculpture: union keeps both, intersection keeps only their agreement, subtraction keeps one at the other's expense. AND, OR and NOT turn out to have volumes, and the torus survives each ruling differently.

booleanvariations.name: booleanvariations
booleanvariations.qfep_connection: Twenty-five recipes for hollowing, perforating and nesting repeat across a 75-cell grid, every result wrapped in a grab cube. Subtraction is the real generator — most of these forms exist only because something was removed, and the wrapper lets you pick the absence up.

boyer_moore.description: Boyer-Moore string search — the algorithm that searches backwards, skipping ahead when mismatches reveal the pattern can't possibly match. Sublinear average time for text search.
boyer_moore.name: Boyer-Moore Pattern Matching
boyer_moore.qfep_connection: The search reads backwards and skips whatever a mismatch proves cannot contain the pattern — efficiency built on ruling text out. Aimed at the word 'queer' in a corpus about trans voices, the mechanism becomes explicit: to be found at all is to survive the skip table.

cave_system.description: Procedural cave generation using noise-based geometry. Random seeds produce unique underground networks — exploration of how controlled randomness creates believable natural spaces.
cave_system.name: Cave System Generator
cave_system.qfep_connection: Seeded noise places and deforms the chambers, but a spanning tree quietly guarantees every cavern connects — the wildness is chaperoned. What reads as geological accident is a connectivity proof wearing rock textures.

closest_pair.description: Closest pair algorithms with divide-and-conquer vs sweep line comparison, dynamic point maintenance, and empirical performance graph
closest_pair.name: Closest Pair of Points
closest_pair.qfep_connection: Nearest-neighbour found twice — recursion's strip against the sweep line's active set — and what gets staged is each method's licensed ignorance: the pairs it can afford never to compare. The performance graph then checks lived milliseconds against O(n log n)'s promise.

context_free_grammars.description: L-system context-free grammar generation and visualization
context_free_grammars.name: Context-Free Grammars
context_free_grammars.qfep_connection: Every string it grows arrives with a receipt — the parse tree hanging face-on in its wall case is the derivation made furniture, controls seated in the body rather than floating beside it. The Chomsky nest states the politics plainly: generative power is graded by what a rewrite rule is permitted to see.

diamondtoruscollection.description: Torus reference ring with hanging cylinders and colored diamonds.
diamondtoruscollection.name: diamondtoruscollection

dijkstra_algorithm.description: Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm — greedy exploration from source, relaxing edges, building the shortest path tree. The foundation of GPS routing and network packet delivery.
dijkstra_algorithm.name: Dijkstra's Algorithm
dijkstra_algorithm.qfep_connection: Certainty grows outward from the source at half-second ticks: each step commits to the cheapest frontier node forever, and the shortest-path tree hardens behind it. Greedy made legible as a temperament — never revisit, never regret.

distance_fields_sdf.name: distance_fields_sdf
distance_fields_sdf.qfep_connection: Every point in the plane carries one number: how far to the nearest surface, negative once you are inside. Sphere-tracing turns looking into a chain of safe steps, and smooth-min quietly abolishes the seam where two shapes were supposed to end.

ecosystem_simulation.description: Predator-prey ecosystem dynamics with emergent population behaviors
ecosystem_simulation.name: Ecosystem Simulation
ecosystem_simulation.qfep_connection: Predator and prey with no referee: populations boom, crash, and circle each other in the phase plane. The swarm chapter at food-web scale — coordination through consequence, the Lotka-Volterra waltz danced by agents who never heard the music.

ecosystem_simulation_2.description: Complex ecosystem with morphology generation, resource systems, and relationship networks
ecosystem_simulation_2.name: Advanced Ecosystem Simulation
ecosystem_simulation_2.qfep_connection: Entities are born as randomized QueerTraits first and only then grown a morphology to fit — identity precedes body, form is derived rather than assigned. And the update loop tends systems, not individuals: resources, boundaries, the relationship network are what actually get a turn each frame.

edmonds_algorithm.capacity: EVALUATE how graph structure enables or blocks pairings and why greedy matching can fall short of the optimum.
edmonds_algorithm.description: Stage the pairing problem that maximum matching tries to solve. The current visualization greedily accepts or skips edges one by one, so you can see how a graph allows some partnerships and strands others. Because the result depends on edge order, the artifact also makes visible why matching needs richer augmenting-path logic than a naive pass. It closes the sequence by turning graph symmetry into the question of who can be paired with whom.
edmonds_algorithm.gamwell_reference: Graph theory, search algorithms, string processing, numerical analysis, optimization theory, critical algorithm studies
interactions: step through candidate pairings edge by edge
watch matched vertices turn green and accepted edges turn red
change edge_density to compare sparse and dense pairing problems
restart to compare different greedy outcomes
edmonds_algorithm.name: Edmonds' Algorithm
edmonds_algorithm.qfep_connection: Pure F as pairing constraint: who can match with whom is determined by the edge pattern, not by any node alone. The greedy pass makes the limits of local choice visible.

entropy_axiom.description: Shannon entropy as foundational axiom — information content measured by surprise. The mathematical bedrock of information theory: uncertainty is quantifiable.
entropy_axiom.name: Entropy Axiom

fetishtorus.description: Parametric dual-torus with fluid shader-driven color cycling and mirror-black contrast. Config: major_radius, minor_radius, ring_count, segment_count, rotation_speed, inner_color_speed, outer_color_speed, gradient_spread, surface_metallic, surface_roughness, dual_torus, second_torus_tilt
fetishtorus.name: Fetish Torus

fibonacci_sequences.description: Recursive mathematical sequences and spiral visualizations
fibonacci_sequences.name: Fibonacci Sequences
fibonacci_sequences.qfep_connection: Recursion in its gentlest clothing: each term the sum of the last two, spiraling into the ratio the golden turn is named for. The sequence that lets nature count without mathematics — phyllotaxis, shells, branching — memory two steps deep, growing a curve.

fluid_simulation.description: Navier-Stokes fluid dynamics visualization — velocity fields, pressure, viscosity, and vorticity. The equations that describe everything from ocean currents to blood flow.
fluid_simulation.name: Fluid Simulation

dna.default: graph=cube - `cube` is the `_` branch of connections_for and returns the twelve-pair literal that was welded into create_graph, in the same order, so the same twelve CSGCylinder3D edges are built between the same node ids. Every other constant is untouched: node_count 8, spring_length 2.0, spring_strength 0.1, repulsion_strength 50.0, damping 0.9, the 10.0 velocity clamp and the 6.0 position bound. layout_seed defaults to 0, and at 0 create_graph issues the same two global randf() calls per node in the same order, so the shipped jitter is bit-identical and two layouts in one room still start differently. warmup_steps defaults to 0, so _ready is the shipped two calls and the graph still starts tangled on its ring and untangles while you watch. time_scale defaults to 1.0, at which dt IS delta and _process is the shipped body. All 9 placements pass no config key - the richest token in the corpus is `force_directed_layout:0:0:0.6` in GT_Layout, which is rotation and y-offset, not config - so the rebuild branch in apply_grid_config is unreachable from every map that exists, and it additionally refuses to fire before the tree is built.
dna.was: no exports at all. Eight plain `var`s, twelve hard-coded connections, and an apply_grid_config whose entire body was `pass`. The runner refused it for NO TURNABLE KNOBS and it was the literal truth. WORTH RECORDING SEPARATELY: this entry's own `interactions` list still tells a reader to 'tune spring_strength and repulsion_strength in exports' and to 'change node_count to alter density'. Those exports have never existed. The claim was false when it was written and it is false now; only `graph` and the three bench knobs are settable, and that is what this block declares.
dna.note: graph is WHICH GRAPH THE SAME FORCE LAW IS ASKED TO DRAW. The description promises that 'clusters, bridges, and peripheral nodes appear as energy redistributes' - a claim about GRAPHS that a single welded adjacency could never test, because with one graph there is nothing for the layout to be a property OF. Every value keeps eight nodes and the identical springs, repulsion, damping and bounds; only the adjacency changes. cube is the shipped twelve pairs, which are the 3-cube Q3: two 4-cycles joined by four rungs, 3-regular and vertex-transitive. ring is C8, eight edges, every node the same degree and no hierarchy anywhere. star is K1,7, a tree, one hub of degree 7 against seven leaves of degree 1 - maximal hierarchy, and the only value with a node that nothing pushes out of the middle. clique is K8, all 28 edges, where there is nothing to reveal because everything is adjacent to everything, and the springs pull it into the tightest blob of the five. bipartite is K4,4, sixteen edges, every one crossing between two classes and none inside either, so the drawing contains no odd cycle at all.
dna.kin: IT IS NOT grid3d_force_directed, and the two must not be read as one family. That token was declined on 2026-08-05 in grid3d.json after considering graph = random|tree|ring|clique|lattice, and its own decline note says so: it runs commons/substrates/grid3d/grid3d_substrate.tscn through cartridge_force_directed.gd, a scene shared by nine tokens, and shares no line with this script. Its blocker does not apply here and the difference is the reason. That force law has NO bounding term, so equilibrium SIZE is set by edge count - the very thing the axis turns - and the dense values photograph as dots inside the sparse ones' frame. This one clamps every position to a 6.0 box in update_positions, and its .tscn additionally carries two fixed indicators at x = -8 and x = +8. So the extent is 12 x 12 at EVERY value (measured: all five settle against the clamp by 240 steps) and the frame is set by furniture that does not move. The union camera is identical for all five here, which is exactly what it could not be there.
dna.still_note: MEASURED by re-implementing the integrator and the harness camera in Python at the rig's real numbers, then rasterising node spheres and edge cylinders. At warmup 480 and framing 5.5: subject 4.67% of frame, peak pairwise 5.39% (clique vs bipartite), weakest pair 2.21% (ring vs star) - every pair over the 2.0% bite threshold. THE FRAMING NUMBER IS LOAD-BEARING AND FRAGILE, and here is why. This artifact is built ENTIRELY from CSG - CSGSphere3D nodes, CSGCylinder3D edges, CSGBox3D indicators - and capture_config_sweep._subtree_aabb counts MeshInstance3D and MultiMeshInstance3D only. It therefore measures NOTHING and falls back to its 1 m default box, which puts the camera 5.4 m from a 17 m object and photographs a 3.3 m window on it. framing 5.5 is calibrated against that fallback box, not against the artifact: it puts the camera at 29.6 m for a 18.1 m frame, and the furthest projected point of any of the five layouts lands at 328 px of the 380 px half-frame. IF ANY MeshInstance3D IS EVER ADDED TO THIS SCENE the fallback stops firing and this number becomes wrong by a factor of eleven. The obvious alternative - a layers=0 anchor sized to the real extent, which is what the brief recommends for this class - was measured and REJECTED: _auto_ground_artifact walks CSGShape3D too, the current min_y of about -4.2 sits just inside its 5.0 m correction cap, and an anchor spanning the true -6.3 would push it over the cap and stop three live placements being lifted at all. The fix for the bench would have been a regression in the maps. THE FIXTURE IS THE REST. warmup_steps=480 runs the shipped integrator at a fixed 1/60 delta so the still is not a fact about frame rate, time_scale=0.0 parks it there, layout_seed=1 pins the starting jitter. relax() deliberately skips update_visuals inside its loop, because every CSG property write rebuilds that shape's mesh.
dna.declines: `path` (P8) was implemented, measured and dropped. It is C8 minus one edge, and under this force law - where 50/d^2 repulsion overwhelms 0.1*(d-2) springs until every node is pressed against the 6.0 clamp - the two settle to layouts 0.31% of frame apart, against a 2.0% threshold. A duplicate tile, and the measurement is why it is not in the list. `stress` - what a node's appearance claims, size|none|heat|degree - was designed and refused on arithmetic. update_visuals scales each node by 1 + min(force * 0.1, 0.5), and at 480 steps the mean residual force is 0.7-2.4, so the scale sits at 1.07-1.24: a 20% radius change on eight small discs that are perhaps a third of a 4.67% subject, which lands near 0.5% of frame. It would ship and return a verdict about the bench. spring_strength, repulsion_strength, damping and spring_length stay plain untyped vars: they set how HARD the same drawing is pulled, and turning them is a dial on one picture. node_count is a density knob and would break the twelve-pair literal that `cube` exists to preserve.
dna.underlying_finding: Two real defects were found on the way and are deliberately NOT papered over by this promotion. The .tscn declares ForceIndicator as a CSGCylinder3D, while setup_indicator_materials fetches it through get_or_create_box_indicator and animate_indicators then guards with `if force_indicator is CSGBox3D` - so the force bar has never once resized in any placement; only the energy bar, which really is a CSGBox3D, responds. And the shipped repulsion has no equilibrium inside the frame: every graph in the family, including the shipped cube, ends pressed flat against the 6.0 clamp within four seconds, so what the room actually shows after a moment is not a force balance but a box holding eight nodes apart. Both are decisions to make, not axes to declare.

force_directed_layout.capacity: READ how attraction, repulsion, and damping turn a tangled network into a stable drawing.
force_directed_layout.description: Watch a tangled graph draw itself. Springs pull linked nodes together while repulsion pushes every pair apart, and the network settles into a readable equilibrium. Node size and indicators make local stress visible, so clusters, bridges, and peripheral nodes appear as energy redistributes. It demonstrates how a legible diagram can emerge from nothing but force balance.
force_directed_layout.gamwell_reference: Graph theory, search algorithms, string processing, numerical analysis, optimization theory, critical algorithm studies
interactions: watch the graph relax toward equilibrium
tune spring_strength and repulsion_strength in exports
change node_count to alter density
reset the scene to compare different random starts
force_directed_layout.name: force_directed_layout
force_directed_layout.qfep_connection: Pure F as relaxation dynamics: attractive and repulsive local laws minimize diagram tension until the graph becomes readable. Structure appears as equilibrium.

forcedirected3d.description: F_repel = k/r^2 (all pairs), F_spring = -k*(L-L0) (edges only). Repulsion spreads nodes apart; springs hold connected nodes together. Layout is equilibrium.
forcedirected3d.name: forcedirected3d

geometric_transformations.description: Animates point, line, plane, and cube primitives through rotation, scale, translation, and shear stages.
geometric_transformations.name: geometric_transformations

parameters.stance: row | stack | ring | origin - where the four primitives stand relative to each other (default row)
parameters.workings: outcome | trace | operands | expression - how much of the operation is drawn (default outcome)

dna.default: stance=row, workings=outcome - the four primitives on the historical x = -6, -2, 2, 6 lineup with nothing drawn but the transformed result, which is exactly what the demo did before promotion, so the 4 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: a lineup along X and a bare outcome, both hard-coded: the base positions were typed three times (setup, translation, shear) as literals, and there was no way to see the operand a matrix acts on, the path it sweeps, or the matrix itself - apply_grid_config was an empty pass
dna.note: stance says what the four dimensions ARE to each other (a vitrine row of separate exhibits, a ladder, an unranked cycle, or one shared vertex cloud at the origin - the artifact's own truth statement, staged). workings shares its word and its four values, in order, with transform_composition_workbench, vector_add and vector_sub

dna.default: basin=bowl, evidence=longhand - longhand is the four trails, the four markers and the four live gradient arrows, i.e. the shipped OPTIMIZERS picture branch for branch; the arrow block is the original code moved under an `if` and nothing else. All 5 existing placements (Cabinet_Gallery, Disposition_Test_Rooms, Grown_DNA_Algorithms, MachineLearning_Evolving_Creatures, ML_Evolution) are plain tokens with no config, so they get exactly what they got before.
dna.was: basin was promoted earlier and lifted function_preset out of apply_grid_config-only reach. What was still hard-coded was the DISCLOSURE: trails, markers and per-runner gradient arrows were drawn unconditionally, so no map could ask this artifact for the answer without the working, or for the rule without the run.
dna.note: evidence is what the artifact offers as proof that a descent happened. result = the four markers alone, an optimizer as a POSITION. trace = + the paths, where SGD's zig-zag, Momentum's overshoot and Adam's straight run actually live - none of that is legible from a marker. longhand = + the local gradient at each runner. axiom = the runners go and -grad f is sampled on the same 9 x 9 lattice the HESSIAN mode reads curvature on, direction normalised (the direction is the local truth the update rule consumes) and length carrying log|grad f| scaled to THIS surface. axiom is where the two axes argue: on plateau every arrow collapses toward the length floor because the surface has nothing to say, and on scarp the columns either side of the face point at each other - both derivatives honest about the bowl, one of them a lie about the cliff between them. The readout and key strip switch with it, because a legend naming four colours none of which is in frame is the label contradicting the picture.
dna.kin: evidence is taken character for character from the family (example_1_7 / 1_9 / 2_8 / 2_9, koch_curve, box_counting_dimension, three_body_problem) - one question asked of a thing in motion: what do you put in the frame as PROOF that a law is moving it? THE DEFAULT DIFFERS FROM THE FAMILY'S. The motion demos ship as `result`, a bare ball with every exhibit withheld; this one ships with its whole working already on the table, so it ships as `longhand`. A map that asks all of them for `longhand` still gets one vocabulary and several answers, which is the test of the shared word.
dna.still_note: evidence needs no rebuild - all four values are branches inside the per-frame ImmediateMesh pass, so apply_grid_config sets the word and never touches the standing 8 m console. Sweeping evidence on the DEFAULT basin (bowl) understates it: bowl's four runners converge to nearly the same short path, so result-vs-trace is small there. Sweep it on `valley` or `plural`, where the trails are long and separate, or measure the pair basin=scarp x evidence=axiom, which is the strongest single frame this artifact can produce.
dna.framing_note: the axis lives in the 8 x 8 m field on the deck, not on the console body, so a fit-by-diagonal that includes the legs and the bay will shrink the field to a fraction of frame. Check subject % before reading any verdict on either axis.

gradient_descent_visualization.description: Gradient descent optimization on a loss landscape — watch the optimizer slide downhill following the steepest direction. The engine behind all neural network training, with learning rate and momentum visible.
gradient_descent_visualization.name: Gradient Descent

graph_coloring.description: Greedy chromatic number exploration on a Petersen graph — 10 nodes colored step-by-step with the lowest available color not used by any neighbor. The four color theorem made visible.
graph_coloring.name: Graph Coloring

graphspace.capacity: WALK a graph as a spatial structure and read how distance, degree, and equilibrium reorganize the network.
graphspace.description: Walk a graph instead of looking at one on paper. Rooms behave as nodes, bridges behave as edges, and a force-directed layout spreads the network until its tensions settle into a navigable form. Dijkstra-based lighting then turns graph distance into atmosphere, so structural centrality is felt as you move. It introduces graph theory as relation made spatial and prepares the sequence's traversal, flow, and connectivity problems.
graphspace.gamwell_reference: Graph theory, search algorithms, string processing, numerical analysis, optimization theory, critical algorithm studies
interactions: walk between rooms as nodes and bridges as edges
change seed to generate a new graph
switch structure_type to assign buildings by degree or distance
set focal_node to recolor the graph by shortest-path distance
graphspace.name: graphspace
graphspace.qfep_connection: Pure F: relation becomes architecture. Force balance reveals a stable spatial form for the graph, letting structure be felt before any traversal or optimization begins.

graphspace3d.name: graphspace3d
graphspace3d.qfep_connection: A graph you inhabit: force-directed layout settles nodes into rooms, edges harden into curved bridges, and any hop past the threshold becomes a teleporter. Edge weight stops being annotation when vertical meters cost your legs more.

homagetothesquare.description: Procedurally layers Albers-inspired colored squares on a plane mesh.
homagetothesquare.name: homagetothesquare

karger_algorithm.description: Randomized algorithm for finding minimum cut in undirected graphs
karger_algorithm.name: Karger's Algorithm

kitbashing.description: Procedural kitbashing — assembling complex forms from randomized geometric primitives. The digital equivalent of the model-making technique used in Star Wars and Blade Runner.
kitbashing.name: Kitbashing
kitbashing.qfep_connection: Coherence is outsourced to the palette: thirty modules assembled without a plan, held together because everything wears the same four theme colors. The bash is random; the kit is the ideology.

koch_curve.description: Classic Koch snowflake fractal curve generation
koch_curve.name: Koch Curve
koch_curve.qfep_connection: The chapter's first miracle, still the cleanest: replace every line's middle third with a tent, repeat. Finite paper, infinite coastline — the Koch curve is where 'dimension' first slips between the integers (log 4 / log 3), and where a student first feels a rule outrun its author.

konigsberg_bridge.description: Euler's Königsberg bridge problem — can you cross every bridge exactly once? The question that birthed graph theory, proving that some problems are about structure, not calculation.
konigsberg_bridge.name: Königsberg Bridge Problem

kosaraju_algorithm.capacity: FOLLOW the two DFS passes and explain why SCCs survive graph transposition.
kosaraju_algorithm.description: Watch the same directed graph answer twice. The first DFS records finishing order, the transpose flips every edge, and the second DFS reveals the strongly connected components that survive reversal. Phase labels and colored passes make the graph's symmetry under transposition visible rather than abstract. It pairs with Tarjan by solving the same problem through a more overt two-pass narrative.
kosaraju_algorithm.gamwell_reference: Graph theory, search algorithms, string processing, numerical analysis, optimization theory, critical algorithm studies
interactions: watch the first and second DFS passes separately
inspect the transposed graph in phase 2
compare SCC colors revealed in reverse finish order
tune edge_density to change component structure
kosaraju_algorithm.name: Kosaraju's Algorithm
kosaraju_algorithm.qfep_connection: Pure F through reversal: transposing the graph changes direction but not mutual reachability. SCCs persist as the invariant structure beneath the two passes.

levenshtein_distance.description: Edit distance visualization — minimum insertions, deletions, and substitutions to transform one string into another. The dynamic programming matrix that powers spell checkers and DNA sequence alignment.
levenshtein_distance.name: Levenshtein Distance
levenshtein_distance.qfep_connection: The DP table prices a transition — 'deadname' to 'chosen_name', every insertion, deletion, and substitution costed at one. What the matrix cannot encode is that the operations were never symmetric for the person performing them.

mst_visualization.capacity: DISTINGUISH necessary from redundant edges in a weighted network and explain why the cheapest backbone works.
mst_visualization.description: Assemble the cheapest skeleton that still keeps the whole graph connected. Kruskal and Prim expose two greedy viewpoints on the same optimization problem: one ranks edges globally, the other grows a tree locally from a root. Accepted edges glow green, rejected cycle-forming edges glow red, and the redundant structure of the full graph becomes legible through what must be left out. The artifact makes efficiency feel like subtraction.
mst_visualization.gamwell_reference: Graph theory, search algorithms, string processing, numerical analysis, optimization theory, critical algorithm studies
interactions: step through edge decisions one by one
switch between Kruskal and Prim
increase edge_density to create more redundant cycles
compare accepted and rejected edges by color
mst_visualization.name: mst_visualization
mst_visualization.qfep_connection: Pure F as optimization: the graph's cheapest connected backbone emerges by stripping away redundant cycles. Necessity becomes visible edge by edge.

network_analysis.capacity: INTERPRET centrality and community structure from motion, glow, and network hierarchy.
network_analysis.description: Read a network as hierarchy, community, and circulation at once. Central nodes orbit slowly and glow more intensely, peripheral nodes move faster at the edges, and pulsing links with particles stage the network as a living system. The visualization turns centrality, clustering, and community structure into spatial rhythm rather than numbers alone. It complements the explicit flow algorithms by building intuition for why some nodes matter more than others.
network_analysis.gamwell_reference: Graph theory, search algorithms, string processing, numerical analysis, optimization theory, critical algorithm studies
interactions: watch hubs, clusters, and peripheral nodes move at different speeds
track flow particles across pulsing edges
set analysis_progress to freeze or amplify the visualization
compare how centrality changes node scale and glow
network_analysis.name: network_analysis
network_analysis.qfep_connection: Pure F as relation and centrality: the artifact reads importance from connection pattern rather than node essence. Community and hub structure become the graph's latent order.

network_flow_visualization.description: Max-flow/min-cut visualization — capacity constraints, augmenting paths, and the duality between maximum flow and minimum cut. The algorithm behind airline scheduling and internet routing.
network_flow_visualization.name: Network Flow
network_flow_visualization.qfep_connection: Augmenting paths push flow until the bottleneck answers back: the maximum a network can carry equals the minimum cut that severs it. Duality staged as capacity politics — what a system delivers is exactly measured by where it can be strangled.

networkflow3d.capacity: IDENTIFY bottlenecks and explain how augmenting paths raise the total flow through a network.
networkflow3d.description: Send flow through a spatial network of pipes. Edmonds-Karp repeatedly finds augmenting paths, particles reveal current flow, and pressure coloring exposes the nodes where capacity is constrained. Elevation penalties make the geometry matter without changing the underlying theorem: max flow is limited by the narrowest cut. It sets up the flow sequence by making bottlenecks visible.
networkflow3d.gamwell_reference: Graph theory, search algorithms, string processing, numerical analysis, optimization theory, critical algorithm studies
interactions: watch augmenting paths fill the network with particles
toggle gravity_effect to penalize uphill capacity
change max_capacity to resize the flow budget
compare source-to-sink bottlenecks by observing pressure colors
networkflow3d.name: networkflow3d
networkflow3d.qfep_connection: F organizes the network while E appears as moving capacity through it. Max-flow min-cut shows where structured routes become constrained by bottlenecks.

newton_raphson_visualization.description: Root-finding by tangent line iteration — each step uses the derivative to leap closer to where the function crosses zero. Quadratic convergence when it works, spectacular chaos when it doesn't.
newton_raphson_visualization.name: Newton-Raphson Method
newton_raphson_visualization.qfep_connection: Trust the tangent completely, land wrong, trust again from where you landed — quadratic convergence is the reward for being mistaken in a rapidly shrinking way. The orange tangent lines archive that faith in linearization; the flat spots where the derivative vanishes are the irreducible the convergence proof never mentions.

pathfinding3d.capacity: COMPARE heuristic strategies by watching how different search rules expand through the same 3D graph.
pathfinding3d.description: Search a voxel maze as if every cube were a graph vertex. The visualization steps A*, Dijkstra, JPS, or flow-field variants through open and closed sets, letting the heuristic shape the visible wavefront. Different heuristics bias the frontier differently, so the artifact makes prediction and optimality visible in space. It turns pathfinding into graph search you can inspect instead of a black box.
pathfinding3d.gamwell_reference: Graph theory, search algorithms, string processing, numerical analysis, optimization theory, critical algorithm studies
interactions: watch the open and closed sets animate through the voxel grid
switch algorithm_type between A*, Dijkstra, JPS, and flow field
change heuristic mode to reshape the frontier
move the start or goal to compare path quality and cost
pathfinding3d.name: pathfinding3d
pathfinding3d.qfep_connection: At the F to E boundary: the graph is fixed, but search explores uncertain futures inside it. Heuristics bias the frontier toward expected order, trading certainty for speed.

pathfinding_visualization.name: pathfinding_visualization
pathfinding_visualization.qfep_connection: Dijkstra run at human speed, frontier and visited cells kept in distinct colors: the cheapest path is assembled only after the algorithm has publicly paid for every cell it considered.

dna.default: staging=pride_room, palette=pride - the shipped code path exactly (10x10 rainbow floor, four banners, six-light ring, pride colours on all nine solids), so the 6 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: zero exports. Nine hand-built polyhedra that always dragged their own room in with them - a rainbow floor plane, four floating banners and a ring of six coloured lights - no matter what room the map had already built; and a declared critical_parameter (the pride_colors array) that no map could reach
dna.note: Declared by hand 2026-07-29; the runner refused it for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. staging asks where the politics lives - in the ROOM the artifact imposes, or in the VERTICES it colours. palette=mono is the honest counterfactual to the artifact's own truth statement 'geometry does not belong to neutrality': same nine solids, same six lights, same floor banding, drained to one grey, so neutrality becomes a value you can select and look at.

platonicsolids.description: Lays out pride-themed platonic solids amid rainbow flooring, banners, and colorful lighting. DNA: staging selects whether the artifact brings its own room (pride_room = rainbow floor + banners + light ring, lit = the coloured light ring only, bare = nine specimens and nothing else); palette selects whose colours the solids, floor bands and lights carry (pride/trans/mono). Use #staging: and #palette:.
platonicsolids.name: platonicsolids

playground_of_joy.description: Playful physics sandbox — interact with bouncy, joyful objects. Physics as play, simulation as delight.
playground_of_joy.name: Playground of Joy
playground_of_joy.qfep_connection: Joy is an explicit float, updated each frame and spent on bounce factor and colour vibrancy, while hand-rolled soft bodies squish by spring rules tuned for delight over accuracy. Affect engineered as parameter — an open admission that playful physics means physics falsified toward pleasure.

pokemon_studio.description: Breeding, growth, and evolution laboratory — grow life from DNA, cross-breed across kingdoms, release into a shared ecosystem
pokemon_studio.name: Pokemon Studio
pokemon_studio.qfep_connection: Growth chamber, breeding lab, and ecosystem joined by a ReleaseGate — the architecture admits that making life and letting it go are separate acts. A LineageTracker writes every cross to disk: even in a toy ecology, ancestry becomes a record that outlives the organism.

push_relabel_algorithm.capacity: EXPLAIN how excess flow and height labels solve max flow without searching complete augmenting paths.
push_relabel_algorithm.description: Treat max flow as local pressure rather than global routes. The source saturates its outgoing edges, nodes accumulate excess, and relabel operations raise heights until flow can keep moving downhill. Watching active nodes flare and heights change makes the algorithm's logic bodily: congestion is stored, redirected, and discharged. It complements Edmonds-Karp by proving that local bookkeeping can solve the same global problem.
push_relabel_algorithm.gamwell_reference: Graph theory, search algorithms, string processing, numerical analysis, optimization theory, critical algorithm studies
interactions: step the algorithm to watch push and relabel operations
inspect height and excess labels on active nodes
compare congested and uncongested states as capacities change
watch sink accumulation become max_flow
push_relabel_algorithm.name: Push-Relabel Algorithm
push_relabel_algorithm.qfep_connection: At the F to E boundary: the network's fixed topology constrains how excess can discharge. Height labels turn structure into a local pressure field for flow.

rainbow.description: Creates double rainbow arcs with atmospheric bloom and layered color bands.

dna.default: banding=roygbiv, substance=light - seven bands at the hard-coded 0.8 thickness and the same unshaded alpha material, so all 5 existing placements are pixel-identical
dna.was: zero exports: a fixed ROYGBIV double arc, Newton's seven bands hard-coded as if the spectrum had seams
dna.note: total arc width is held constant across banding, so the knob argues about how many names the spectrum gets, not how big it is; substance turns an optical event with no location into an arch that could hold a shadow, which contradicts the artifact's own truth line on purpose

rainbow.name: rainbow

remains_to_be_seen.description: Critical theory artifact exploring visibility, erasure, and what computation makes invisible. What the algorithm chooses not to show is as important as what it reveals.
remains_to_be_seen.name: Remains To Be Seen
remains_to_be_seen.qfep_connection: After Hatoum: wireframe furniture hung in a grid with roughly a third of positions randomly skipped, the whole field swinging slightly. The gaps do the mourning — what the loop declines to place reads as what was taken, and the slow sway keeps absence from settling into pattern.

rorschach_monitor.description: Medical monitor displaying animated Rorschach brain scan layers
rorschach_monitor.name: Rorschach Monitor
rorschach_monitor.qfep_connection: The same mirrored noise, now institutionalized: a bezel, an emissive screen, and four palettes named CT, MRI, PET, Thermal. Diagnosis as colourway — the data never changes, only the clinical costume that makes it read as medicine.

rorschach_scan.description: Animated mirrored inkblot pattern like a brain CT scan
rorschach_scan.name: Rorschach Brain Scan
rorschach_scan.qfep_connection: Simplex noise thresholded, then mirrored across the midline and scanned through sixty-four layers like a CT: the mirror is the entire apparatus. Bilateral symmetry is what recruits your projection — the machine guarantees only the reflection, you supply the moth.

rsa_visualization.description: RSA public-key cryptography visualization — prime factorization, modular exponentiation, and the one-way trapdoor that makes secure communication possible. Easy to multiply primes, nearly impossible to factor back.
rsa_visualization.name: RSA Encryption
rsa_visualization.qfep_connection: Secrecy staged as asymmetry of effort: the sieve turns up p and q in seconds on a ten-by-ten grid, while their product sits there daring anyone to factor it back. Green for public, red for private — the trapdoor's politics is that multiplication is cheap and its inverse is a life sentence.

running_text_display.description: Scrolling text display for critical theory — words flowing through space, text as material, reading as embodied spatial practice.
running_text_display.name: Running Text Display
running_text_display.qfep_connection: A Holzer truism on an emissive box: the sentence is rendered in a hidden viewport and dragged past pixel by pixel, so reading happens at the display's tempo, not yours. Text as duration — you cannot skim what owns its own clock.

scale_me.capacity: FEEL uniform scaling as a change in bodily reference rather than a numeric ratio.
scale_me.description: A grab sphere that rescales the world around the player. The geometry keeps its proportions, but your reference body changes, so scale becomes something felt rather than merely calculated. That shift makes the same room read as intimate, toy-like, or monumental without changing its form. It is scale as embodiment.
scale_me.gamwell_reference: Graph theory, search algorithms, string processing, numerical analysis, optimization theory, critical algorithm studies
interactions: grab the trigger sphere to rescale the world
compare the room before and after the scale shift
adjust scale_amount to test subtle versus monumental change
wait for the automatic reset to compare embodied reference frames
scale_me.name: scale_me
scale_me.qfep_connection: Pure S through uniform scaling: ratios are preserved while the reference frame changes. Identity survives, but the felt relation between body and world is transformed.

dna.default: cue=trace - trace resolves through _mode_for_cue() to STIGMERGY, which is the mode _mode was hard-pinned to before the promotion, so all 10 existing placements open on the deposit heatmap they already opened on. Draws come off one seeded _rng (BUILD_SEED) rather than the global stream, and seed()/randomize() is never called, so the artifact neither consumes nor reseeds the process-wide RNG other artifacts in the same map are drawing from.
dna.was: no axis of its own. _mode was pinned to STIGMERGY and the other two modes were reachable only by pressing MODE in the headset - an artifact built to argue that order has three possible sources shipped exactly one of them to every map and every capture. The MODE button now walks `cue` rather than going behind it, so the headset and the map token cannot disagree about what is on screen.
dna.note: NOT the reaction_diffusion inert class. The three values are not three parameter settings of one field - they change which readout is built and where. `neighbour` clears the centre plate and adds a 2.0 x 4.8 m phase graph at x -5.5..-3.5, two metres of geometry no other value builds and on the opposite side of the body; `trace` and `slope` build the right-hand order bar that `neighbour` removes. The differences are gross layout, not fine texture, so they survive a still. A fourth no-medium value (all coupling off, empty field) was considered and cut: a blank plate is how a render scores INERT, and it is not an argument.

self_organizing_patterns.description: Stigmergy, phase transitions, and attractor basin visualization — 3 modes: stigmergy field with deposit/evaporation heatmap, Ising-like phase transition with order parameter sweep, Voronoi-colored attractor basins with flow field arrows
self_organizing_patterns.name: Self-Organizing Patterns
self_organizing_patterns.qfep_connection: Three windows on order-from-below: a stigmergy field where deposits recruit deposits, phase transitions where a parameter nudge flips the regime, attractor basins where histories converge. The theory shelf of the chapter — why local rules don't just make patterns, but make *stable* ones.

simulated_annealing.description: Adaptive thermal optimization with basin-hopping — ImmediateMesh energy landscape, acceptance probability distribution, adaptive cooling rate targeting optimal acceptance, and basin-hopping to escape local minima.
simulated_annealing.name: Simulated Annealing
simulated_annealing.qfep_connection: The escape from the merely-nearby minimum: heat the system so it can jump out of shallow valleys, then cool it slowly so it settles into a deep one. Basin-hopping on an energy landscape, borrowed from how metals find their strongest crystal. The chapter's answer to descent's blindness — sometimes to find the best shape you must first let the form shake.

dna.default: basin=plural, evidence=longhand - plural short-circuits to the shipped problem_type 'rastrigin' WITHOUT WRITING IT: _sync_basin_from_exports only assigns problem_type when basin is something other than its default, so the objective string, the height range, the mesh and the colours are the same objects built by the same code as before. evidence=longhand is the shipped picture branch for branch - trail, both markers, hop marks, the P(accept) histogram and both working label lines - and _apply_evidence deliberately draws nothing itself, so the default does not even move the histogram's first frame. All five placements (Cabinet_Gallery, FormFinding_Annealing, Gallery_Misc, Gallery_Misc_Placed, Placement_Simulated_Annealing) are BARE tokens with no #key:value, and GridInteractablesComponent only calls apply_grid_config when merged_config is non-empty, so none of them reaches the new code at all. The two fixture exports default to 0 and 0, which are 'leave the global RNG alone' and 'run nothing early'.
dna.was: no declared axis - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Twenty-eight exports existed and every one was a temperature, a rate, a count or a dimension; the one categorical knob, problem_type, was a bare String with its four legal values in a trailing COMMENT, reachable only by typing the exact word. apply_grid_config read fourteen keys and then, unconditionally on ANY call, tore the console and the control panel down, re-cut them, threw the search away and started a new one - the force_pad trap, dormant only because no token has ever carried a key.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05. basin is gradient_descent_visualization's word and its five values, character for character, and taking it is the point rather than a convenience: annealing and descent are the same picture - a runner on a relief - differing in exactly one thing, that this one is allowed to move UPHILL. That licence is meaningless on a bowl and is the only way out of an egg-crate, so the argument does not exist until the surface is named. A map that asks both tables for the same basin gets one landscape and two policies on it, which is the comparison neither can make alone. TWO OF THE FIVE FORMULAS ARE THE SIBLING'S UNTOUCHED (bowl = x^2+y^2, valley = the same Rosenbrock) and scarp is ported from it below; plural and plateau are served by THIS artifact's own shipped Rastrigin and Ackley instead of the sibling's Himmelblau and tanh disc, because both are textbook members of the class the word names and because swapping them in would have discarded the default this artifact ships with. Where the functions differ the word still means the same thing. evidence is the same four rungs the motion family uses, asked here of a search that is permitted to be wrong on purpose.
dna.scarp_note: THE RISE IS THE FAMILY'S PROPORTION, NOT ITS NUMBER. gradient_descent fixes a 3.0 step against a bowl spanning 2*4^2 = 32 over its domain and renders it with a per-function y_scale; this artifact normalises every relief over its own measured min/max, so a literal 3.0 against a domain-5 bowl spanning 50 would flatten to two thirds of the sibling's contrast and read as `bowl` with a smudge on it. SCARP_RATIO = 3/32 reproduces the ratio at whatever search_space_size is set to. Since the surface is coloured by normalised height, the whole x>0 half of the plate shifts band - this should be the loudest value on the axis, and if it is not, suspect the capture and not the function.
dna.still_note: EVERY RUNG OF BOTH AXES IS STANDING GEOMETRY, but the walk that draws three of evidence's four is not standing yet when the shutter opens. The bench settles 1.1 s, step_interval is 0.06, and _process performs at most ONE step per frame whatever step_interval says - so an unpinned capture photographs about eighteen steps of a thousand: a stub of trail, an almost-empty histogram, no basin hops (stagnation_threshold is 80) and nothing rejected. result / trace / longhand would then differ by a few centimetres of line and the axis would read INERT as a fact about the shutter. prerun_steps runs the search forward synchronously in _ready; anneal_seed pins the whole thing, without which four basin frames differ by the surface AND by four unrelated random walks drawn over it. The temperature schedule itself is NOT an axis and cannot be: cooling is the one thing this artifact does that a still cannot hold.
dna.framing_note: unchecked against a capture in this pass. The axis lives in a 1.4 m plate that is 0.15 m deep in relief, the sweep camera sits at pitch -0.26 rad, and _create_console now stands the whole thing on a 0.90 m deck with a rail ring and a control pad - so a fit-by-diagonal sees a near-edge-on plate inside a much taller box. Deliberately NOT given a dna.framing number here: the identical geometry on gradient_descent_visualization carries the same warning and no number, and inventing one without a frame to check it against would be guessing at two artifacts at once. Check subject % before reading any verdict on either axis.

small_world_network.description: Watts-Strogatz small-world model — 20 nodes in a ring lattice with k=4 neighbors. VR slider controls rewiring probability p: regular lattice at p=0, random graph at p=1. Watch how random shortcuts collapse average path length while clustering stays high. Gray edges are original, yellow edges are rewired shortcuts.
small_world_network.name: Small World Network
small_world_network.qfep_connection: Drag p and yellow shortcuts replace gray lattice edges: a handful of rewired links collapses the ring's path length while clustering barely moves. Six degrees turns out to be cheap — the small world costs almost nothing over the regular one.

tarjan_algorithm.capacity: TRACE low-link propagation and see where directed cycles collapse into strongly connected components.
tarjan_algorithm.description: Follow a single depth-first pass as it discovers strongly connected components. Discovery times, low-link values, and the stack make cycles visible as pockets of mutual reachability that pop out in reverse traversal order. Back edges show exactly where a directed graph folds back on itself, and each component flashes into view when its root condition is met. It teaches SCCs as something you can watch emerge, not just compute.
tarjan_algorithm.gamwell_reference: Graph theory, search algorithms, string processing, numerical analysis, optimization theory, critical algorithm studies
interactions: watch DFS visit vertices one step at a time
track back edges and low-link updates
compare sparse and dense directed graphs via edge_density
read component colors as SCCs pop from the stack
tarjan_algorithm.name: Tarjan's Algorithm
tarjan_algorithm.qfep_connection: Pure F in directed form: SCCs mark the regions where reachability closes back on itself. Low-link values reveal hidden cycles inside apparent sequence.

tartan_demo.description: Loads the tartan boxes showcase with bright shader-driven crates under studio lighting.
tartan_demo.name: tartan_demo
tartan_demo.qfep_connection: A hundred crates, one shader, one seeded integer apiece: the difference between clan and clan is a grid index times 47.3, routed into five preset happy palettes. Tartan's whole heraldry of belonging, recompiled as a random number generator under studio bloom.

topological_sort_algorithm.description: Algorithm for ordering vertices in directed acyclic graphs
topological_sort_algorithm.name: Topological Sort
topological_sort_algorithm.qfep_connection: Kahn's algorithm in color: a vertex may act only when its in-degree reaches zero, freedom defined as having no remaining obligations. Making dependency visible also makes hierarchy visible — the level bands are a caste diagram for tasks.

tree_generation.description: Procedural tree generation using L-system algorithms
tree_generation.name: Tree Generation
tree_generation.qfep_connection: One rule, F to F[+F]F[-F]F, applied six times, and a sentence grows into a tree. The bracket is the whole trick: push and pop give the linear string a memory of where it branched — recall is what makes growth spatial.

voronoi_visualization.name: voronoi_visualization
voronoi_visualization.qfep_connection: Territory as nearest-neighbour arithmetic: every point of the plane pledges to its closest site until nothing is unclaimed, the Fortune sweep performing the annexation live. POWER mode leaks the politics — weight a site and its cell swells, borders redrawn by an invisible coefficient.

topological_sort.description: Topological sort — linear ordering of vertices in a directed acyclic graph
topological_sort.qfep_connection: The DAG's confession: once arrows forbid cycles, some order becomes mandatory. Topological sort extracts the hidden queue inside any dependency web — what must come before what — and shows that a graph without loops is secretly a to-do list. In the connectivity room it stands opposite Tarjan and Kosaraju: they find the cycles, it lives where cycles are outlawed.

wiki_fragment.description: A deliberately incomplete reading panel. Each fragment ends with a cross-reference to another fragment elsewhere in the room — and the chain cycles. No one panel carries the thesis. Walking the four of them does. Enacts the commons as response to incompleteness: what one editor cannot hold, the ledger can.
wiki_fragment.name: Wiki Fragment

identity.essence: A claim that admits it needs the others
identity.desire: To be read as one of four, never alone
identity.truth: No node is true alone. A wiki is not consistent; it is corrigible — which is more honest.

situated_readout.description: A flat display panel showing a classification verdict for the same SUBJECT #4729. The verdict is determined by the panel's own world position — place four instances in four quadrants and the player sees four incompatible 'objective' answers to the same query. Haraway's situated knowledge, enacted spatially: the view always comes from somewhere.
situated_readout.name: Situated Readout

identity.essence: A verdict that changes with where it speaks from
identity.desire: To be read alongside three siblings showing incompatible answers to the same input
identity.truth: There is no view from nowhere — the classification belongs to the location, not the subject

registry_info.description: Standalone algorithm artifacts spanning graph theory, search/pathfinding, string algorithms, numerical methods, optimization, cryptography, and critical theory. Algorithms that don't yet have their own registry family.
registry_info.name: algorithms_misc
registry_info.theoretical_grounding: Graph theory, search algorithms, string processing, numerical analysis, optimization theory, critical algorithm studies
